stem.text: The function \( f \) has derivatives of all orders for all real \( x \). Selected values of \( f \) and its first four derivatives at \( x = 2 \) are given in the table. \[ \begin{array}{c|ccccc} x & f(x) & f'(x) & f''(x) & f'''(x) & f^{(4)}(x) \\ \hline 2 & 3 & -4 & 6 & -18 & 48 \end{array} \]

parts.prompt: Write the third-degree Taylor polynomial for \( f \) about \( x = 2 \).

worked_solution.text: Divide each derivative by the matching factorial.

points.criterion: Writes the first two nonzero terms, 3 and -4(x - 2), in a list or as part of a polynomial.
Completes the polynomial 3 - 4(x - 2) + 3(x - 2)^2 - 3(x - 2)^3, with 6/2! = 3 and -18/3! = -3, with no term of degree above 3; any algebraically equivalent polynomial is accepted.

parts.prompt: Write the third-degree Taylor polynomial for \( f' \) about \( x = 2 \).

worked_solution.text: The derivatives of f' at 2 are f'(2), f''(2), f'''(2) and f^(4)(2).

points.criterion: Writes the first two nonzero terms, -4 and 6(x - 2), in a list or as part of a polynomial.
Completes the polynomial -4 + 6(x - 2) - 9(x - 2)^2 + 8(x - 2)^3, with no term of degree above 3; any algebraically equivalent polynomial is accepted.

parts.prompt: Let \( h(x) = \displaystyle\int_{2}^{x} f(t)\,dt \). Write the fourth-degree Taylor polynomial for \( h \) about \( x = 2 \).

worked_solution.text: h(2) = 0 and h' = f, so the derivatives of h at 2 are 0, 3, -4, 6 and -18.

points.criterion: Writes the first two nonzero terms, 3(x - 2) and -2(x - 2)^2, in a list or as part of a polynomial; a nonzero constant term does not earn the point.
Writes the third-degree term (x - 2)^3, from f''(2)/3! = 6/6.
Completes the polynomial 3(x - 2) - 2(x - 2)^2 + (x - 2)^3 - (3/4)(x - 2)^4, with no term of degree above 4; any algebraically equivalent polynomial is accepted.

parts.prompt: Let \( k(x) = f(2 + x^{2}) \). Write the sixth-degree Taylor polynomial for \( k \) about \( x = 0 \).

worked_solution.text: Replace x - 2 by x^2 in the third-degree polynomial from part (a); higher terms of f have degree above 6.

points.criterion: Writes the first two nonzero terms, 3 and -4x^2, in a list or as part of a polynomial.
Completes the polynomial 3 - 4x^2 + 3x^4 - 3x^6, with no term of degree above 6 (in particular no 2x^8 term); any algebraically equivalent polynomial is accepted.
